items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Actions that reduce the sources or enhance the sinks of greenhouse gases, such as renewable energy, energy efficiency and reforestation"?
items.answer: mitigation

items.stem: Explain why direct air capture is controversial as a mitigation strategy.
items.answer: It is very expensive (about US$400-1,000 per tonne) and energy-intensive; capacity is tiny (thousands of tonnes vs ~37 billion tonnes emitted); it may create moral hazard, delaying emissions cuts.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It is very expensive (about US$400-1,000 per tonne) and energy-intensive; capacity is tiny (thousands of tonnes vs ~37 billion tonnes emitted); it may create moral hazard, delaying emissions cuts. items.stem: Distinguish between a carbon tax and a cap-and-trade (emissions trading) scheme.
items.answer: A carbon tax sets the price of carbon and lets the quantity emitted vary; cap-and-trade sets the quantity (cap) and lets the market determine the price of allowances (e.g. EU ETS).
items.markingKey: A carbon tax sets the price of carbon and lets the quantity emitted vary; cap-and-trade sets the quantity (cap) and lets the market determine the price of allowances (e.g. EU ETS). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.answer: Continued fossil-fuel dependence and new investment; insufficient national targets (NDCs) and weak implementation; rising energy demand in developing economies; political resistance.

items.stem:

items.answer: A high, predictable price shifted heating from oil to district heating and biomass, decoupling growth from emissions.

items.stem: The remaining carbon budget for 1.5 °C (50% probability) is about 500 Gt CO₂ and global emissions are 37.4 Gt CO₂ per year. (a) Calculate how long the budget would last at constant emissions. (b) If emissions instead fall linearly to zero, calculate the year by which net zero must be reached (start in 2025). (c) Per-capita emissions in Nigeria are about 0.4 t CO₂. Discuss how the remaining budget could be shared fairly between countries.
items.answer: (a) 13.4 years (b) area of triangle: 500 = 37.4 × n / 2 → n = 26.7 years → net zero by about 2052 (c) approaches include equal per-capita shares, historical responsibility (high-income countries emitted most cumulative CO₂), capability to pay, and the right to development; Nigeria's per-capita emissions of 0.4 t compared with a world average of about 4.7 t illustrate unequal responsibility.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 13.4. (b) M1 triangle area, A1 ≈ 2052. (c) R1 equity principle, R1 use of per-capita data / common but differentiated responsibilities.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "managed retreat"?
options: The planned relocation of people and infrastructure away from areas at risk, such as eroding coasts
The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, opened for signature at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, whose parties meet at annual Conferences of the Parties (COPs)
A country's self-set climate action plan and emissions target under the Paris Agreement, updated every five years

items.stem: Explain the difference between soft (ecosystem-based) adaptation and hard engineering adaptation.
items.answer: Hard engineering uses built structures (sea walls, flood barriers such as the Thames Barrier) that are costly and inflexible; soft adaptation works with natural processes (mangrove restoration, managed retreat, floodplain restoration).

items.stem: The remaining carbon budget for 2 °C (67% probability) is about 1150 Gt CO₂ and global emissions are 36.8 Gt CO₂ per year. items.answer: (a) 31.3 years (b) area of triangle: 1150 = 36.8 × n / 2 → n = 62.5 years → net zero by about 2088 (c) approaches include equal per-capita shares, historical responsibility (high-income countries emitted most cumulative CO₂), capability to pay, and the right to development; Germany's per-capita emissions of 7.6 t compared with a world average of about 4.7 t illustrate unequal responsibility.
